**Answer: 36**

**Interpretation.** The example says a single lit button always gives the same observation, wherever it is. So the student cannot see the panel's frame. They see only the lit pattern, which is the same up to translation. Two lit patterns look identical exactly when one is a translate of the other.

**Counting.** Each observable arrangement is a nonempty set of cells whose bounding box is exactly $a \times b$, with $1 \le a \le 3$ rows and $1 \le b \le 2$ columns. Let $N(a,b)$ be the number of subsets of an $a\times b$ grid that meet every row and every column.

- $N(1,1)=1$
- $N(1,2)=1$ (both cells)
- $N(2,1)=1$ (both cells)
- $N(2,2)=7$: the full set (1), the four 3-cell sets, and the two diagonal pairs (the other pairs leave a row or column empty)
- $N(3,1)=1$ (all three cells)
- $N(3,2)=25$: each of the 3 rows is nonempty, giving $3^3=27$ choices; subtract the 2 choices that miss a column entirely (all rows use only the left column, or only the right column)

Summing gives $1+1+1+7+1+25 = 36$.

**Check.** A single lit button gives exactly one arrangement, which matches the example.

ANSWER: 36
